scope: Focused comparison for P46 revision 1.1, not exhaustive priority certification

sources.source: Gallo, Mosconi, Squassina, Power law convergence and concavity for the logarithmic Schrodinger equation
sources.version: Final author-hosted 60-page article; Mathematische Annalen 395 (2026), article 21
sources.read_this_turn: Final p.44 explicit ball question and surrounding one-dimensional calculation; arXiv v2 introduction on normalized transform and general log-concavity
sources.finding: The original named question concerns balls. The new deformation result answers the subsequent question in the published P46 Section 7; it is not falsely attributed as a general-domain conjecture of GMS.

sources.source: Ishige, Salani, Takatsu, New characterizations of log-concavity
sources.read_this_turn: Definitions and Section 4.2, pp.17-19, including the small-rescaling class and terminology comparison
sources.finding: Small-rescaling half-log-concavity is distinct from normalization at the maximum. No preservation theorem is contradicted or used as a PDE proof input.

sources.source: Ishige, Salani, Takatsu, To logconcavity and beyond
sources.finding: Older reciprocal-exponent terminology also permits all sufficiently small multiplicative factors. Metadata was not used to conflate it with the cusp normalization.

sources.source: Knezevic and Suli, Spectral Galerkin approximation of Fokker-Planck equations with unbounded drift
sources.read_this_turn: Theorem 2.1 and Corollary 2.2 on printed p.450, with reference attribution to Bobkov and Ledoux
sources.finding: Classical Brascamp-Lieb weighted variance inequality on convex open sets. The needed smooth-ball exhaustion argument is supplied in the new proof.

sources.source: Gallo, Moraschi, Squassina, Quantitative and exact concavity principles for parabolic and elliptic equations
sources.read_this_turn: Relevant extracted log-concavity and constant-rank passages, including Corollary 5.3; not all 41 pages
sources.finding: Ordinary log-concavity and parabolic concavity statements do not supply the normalized-maximum deformation theorem in the inspected passages.
